introduce-presubmit-orchestrator-ci-telemetry-and-dep-hint-linter

Context: As the repo has grown, presubmit hooks have accumulated ad-hoc ordering and duplicated setup costs across multiple language runners.

This caused noisy flakiness in CI, slow feedback for small changes, and sprawl in scripts maintained across teams.

Motivation: unify presubmit sequencing, surface CI-level telemetry (duration, cache hit/miss, matrix cardinality), and provide early guidance for dependency hygiene so engineers remove unnecessary devDependencies during PRs.

Summary of changes: 1) Add a small Go-based presubmit-orchestrator (ci/orchestrator/) that defines ordered hook groups (setup, lint, unit, integration-smoke).

It exposes a declarative manifest (ci/presubmit.yaml) that can be updated per-repo or per-path glob.

2) Introduce ci/telemetry-exporter: a lightweight helper that emits metrics (presubmit.duration_ms, cache.hit, test.flaky_count) to our internal telemetry endpoint and as a debug artifact in artifacts/ci-telemetry.json.

3) Dependency-hint linter (tools/dep-hint) that statically analyzes package manifests (package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml) and heuristically flags devdeps that are not referenced by tooling paths in the patch.

4) Split lint runners into language-aware shards (ts-lint, go-lint, py-lint) and wire adaptive caching so only affected shards run by default.

5) Add a staged release hook that enforces a lightweight smoke test (release/smoke.sh) before promoting artifacts to the release pipeline.

Migration steps: - No required action for developers.

The orchestrator autodetects existing hook files and migrates them into the new manifest where safe; teams will get a migration PR in their subpackages if the heuristics are uncertain. - To opt out of telemetry, set ci/telemetry.yaml.disable: true in repo root. - Dep-hint linter can be disabled per-path with .dep-hint-ignore.

Testing & validation: - Local unit tests for orchestrator and dep-hint included (ci/test/orchestrator_test.go, tools/dep-hint/tests/). - Ran presubmit smoke across core packages (redwood/, redwood-sdk-python/, redwood-helm-charts/) with representative patches. - Nightly run enabled for 48 hours in the feature branch to capture telemetry before merge.

Rollout & safety: - Feature gated under repo-level flag ci.presubmit.orchestrator.enabled; turned on for main by this PR after a 7-day telemetry observation window. - Fallback: if orchestrator fails, the old scripts are executed (compat shim at ci/compat/). - Performance: median presubmit wall time reduced ~18% in observed workloads; cold-cache improvements from targeted shard execution reduced setup time by ~25%.

CI details & history: - Initial run (workflow: presubmit/main) failed due to a flaky test in integrations/smoke (flake count: 1).

Reproduced locally, added a small timeout backstop and retriggered. - Second run succeeded; telemetry exporter produced artifacts/ci-telemetry.json with aggregated bucketed latencies. - Lint stage produced actionable hints for ~27 open PRs across org (most common: unused jest-devtools and stale ts-node entries in package.json).

Security considerations: - Telemetry exporter only sends aggregated numeric metrics and anonymized job tags; no source code or secrets.

It is behind an allowlist and uses existing CI tokens with restricted scope. - Dep-hint linter is read-only and runs in CI; it does not modify manifests automatically.

Implementation notes: - The orchestrator is intentionally small (~900LOC Go) to keep startup deterministic.

It uses a manifest-driven model to allow future per-team tweaks without code changes. - Adaptive shard selection uses path globs and a cached mapping at .ci/cache/shard-map.json which is updated by a periodic job. - Added documentation in docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md and a migration guide docs/dev/dep-hint.md.

Related: ENG-4287 (presubmit orchestration), ENG-4290 (ci telemetry), SUP-214 incident notes on flaky presubmits.

compat(openai): partial-dispatch support for streaming tool_choice + graceful fallback and schema alignment

Context: OpenAI-style tool/function calling remains a major integration point for customer workloads.

We observed two recurring issues in the compatibility shim: 1) long-running streaming responses where the model decides on a tool mid-stream (partial tool_choice) produced inconsistent framing and occasionally caused client disconnects; 2) when a tool schema in the compatibility catalog diverged slightly from the model's schema name/shape, the runtime fell back too aggressively to text output, losing structured output semantics.

This PR introduces a targeted compatibility layer to make partial tool_choice streaming first-class and to perform tolerant schema alignment during handoff.

Summary of changes: - Streaming protocol: emit explicit tool_choice.hint frames and tool_choice.commit frames in the OpenAI-framed event stream so downstream SDKs (TS/Python/Go) can render an in-progress tool invocation UI and then commit when the model decides.

Hints are non-terminal and include a suggested tool id + partial args payload (encrypted/hashed if configured). - Fallback semantics: add a new policy 'graceful_invoke_fallback' which, if the selected tool is unavailable or schema-mismatched, continues streaming the tool invocation envelope (function-call style) instead of abruptly switching to plain text.

This preserves structured output and allows clients to present a retry UI or queue the invocation. - Schema alignment: introduce schema similarity matching (name aliasing, field-level relaxed matching, and a best-effort mapping layer) at the dispatcher so small mismatches don't force a textual fallback.

The mapping is conservative by default and opt-in via the compatibility config. - Backwards compatibility: the new frames are additive and ignored by older clients; we added a registry flag to disable hints for customers who want strict parity. - Tests & CI: unit tests for the dispatcher and decoder, integration test that reproduces the previous regression with partial tool_choice across a streaming boundary, and e2e with the TS SDK to assert the commit frame ordering.

Motivation: these changes reduce incidents where user-facing apps lost structured tool call semantics mid-stream and improves developer experience for SDK consumers of the OpenAI compatibility layer.

Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller for Model Version Lifecycle

Context and motivation: Rolling model versions safely at scale requires more than traffic splitting — it requires cohort-based swaps that respect downstream dependencies, per-cohort evaluation windows, and automated rollback when service-level guards fail. This PR introduces the Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller (CPSC), a controller in the rollout orchestration layer that performs swap-style rollouts by progressing model versions cohort-by-cohort rather than sample-level splits.

Goals: reduce exposure of regressions, preserve cold-start isolation, enable dependency-aware health checks (datastore schema, adapter compatibility), and provide deterministic swap semantics for auditability.

High-level design:
- Cohorts are lightweight tagged slices of users (by tenant, georegion, or feature flag).

Evacuation timestamp synchronizer and soft-threshold hedge (hotfix)

Background: During a regional overload incident we observed two problematic behaviors: (1) concurrent node-level evacuations in the same cohort sometimes used slightly different evacuation timestamps, which allowed a small window where tenant leases were double-counted for eviction heuristics, causing unnecessary churn; (2) the soft-threshold path that should temporarily relax SLO enforcement while preserving KV prefix cache was too aggressive when combined with speculative prefetch, causing higher tail-latency for critical tenants.

This PR introduces a lightweight cross-region evacuation timestamp synchronizer (best-effort, clock-drift tolerant) and a hedging mechanism that gates the soft-threshold relaxation when coordinated prefetch is active.

The goal is to reduce false-positive evictions and preserve high-priority tenant latency during transient overloads.

What this changes: - Introduces EvacTS protocol: a compact lease-synchronization envelope sent during evacuation orchestration that attaches a monotonic evacuation-id + origin-hash and a micro-timestamp (millis).

Implemented as best-effort: nodes will accept and reconcile newer evacuation-ids from upstream controllers; older messages are ignored.

This avoids races where two controllers start overlapping evacuations with different epoch anchors. - Adds a soft-threshold hedge: the SLO relaxer now consults a lightweight prefetch-state predicate.

If prefetch activity for a tenant exceeds a threshold and eviction pressure is marginal, the relaxer defers full soft-mode and instead applies a graded limit (50%-80% of the intended relaxation) to protect tail latency. - Telemetry: emits evac_ts.accepted, evac_ts.rejected (by-staleness), soft_hedge.applied, and soft_hedge.skipped; updated dashboards with example alert queries included in docs/telemetry/playbooks.md - Backwards compatibility: EvacTS is backward-compatible: older nodes ignore unknown fields; controllers will fall back to existing behavior if no evacuationsync ACKs are observed. - Rollout plan: staged rollout to regional controllers (canary region -> 3 additional regions -> global) with a 1-hour observation window per stage.

Fix severity: high (incident-driven hotfix).

Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have accumulated long-running lint shards and a growing transitive dependency surface that slows feedback and increases CI cost.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight Go-based dependency pruner (dep-pruner) run as a pre-merge check that detects and optionally removes unused devdeps/transitive entries from package manifests and (2) a stage-aware lint orchestrator action that re-groups lint shards into fast/medium/slow lanes with an adaptive fastpath for small PRs.

Goals: reduce presubmit latency, shrink devdep churn, and provide a safe rollout path for lint reshuffling.

temporal-affinity-refill-and-scavenger-for-paged-kv

Summary: Introduces a temporal-affinity driven refill strategy and a light-weight scavenger for the paged KV cache to reduce tail latency in continuous-batching workloads. The change combines a small per-block temporal score, a refill iterator that biases reuse toward recently accessed neighborhoods, and a background scavenger that reclaims cold blocks in low-contention phases.

Motivation: production traces showed frequent cold-evictions followed by immediate re-loads in chat-heavy workloads (p95 token latency spikes during bursty sessions). Existing LRU-like eviction was brittle under small working sets per shard; this PR aims to reduce re-fetch churn and improve p95 latency while keeping allocation fast and allocator lock contention low.

Design:
- Temporal affinity score: each block maintains a u8 score incremented on reuse and decayed on periodic ticks. Score affects refill priority but is cheap to read/write (atomic u8 ops).
- Refill iterator: when a request misses, the allocator first probes the local page neighborhoods ordered by temporal score to prefer reuse of recently-warmed blocks (improves KV cache hit-locality for streaming sessions).
- Scavenger thread: a low-priority background worker scans age-buckets and coalesces contiguous cold blocks for efficient reclamation. It only runs when heap pressure is below a configurable threshold to avoid interfering with latency-sensitive fast-paths.
- Fast-path admit/evict: a non-blocking admit path reserves a hot-slot for short windows to avoid ABA churn when multiple fibers are refilling the same keys. Contention fallback uses a short spin-and-yield policy.

Compatibility: no changes to on-disk layout or RPCs; config knobs exposed via runtime flags for decay interval and scavenger thresholds.

- [x] Unit tests for refill iterator determinism

Testing and results:
- Unit and integration tests: all passing locally and in CI.
- Benchmarks (kv_batch_bench): p95 generation latency reduced by 18% on a 4-GPU dedicated worker under synthetic chat sessions with 60s bursts. Tail behavior improved: p99 reduced by ~12%.
- Memory churn: observed working set re-loads reduced by ~22% in flamegraphs; CPU overhead of scavenger measured at <1% on average.

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased metadata (per-block score): limited to +1 byte per block; accounted for in allocator sizing.
- Scavenger interfering with latency: runs only when allocator free-pages > threshold and its work budget is capped per tick.
- Contention on fast-path: fallback path in allocator uses adaptive backoff.

Introduce session-windowed latency sketches and invocation replaybench

Motivation: token-level and per-invocation metrics currently provide high-cardinality point traces that make it hard to understand session-level latency behavior (bursty tails, intra-session skew) without expensive trace rehydration. This PR adds compact, session-windowed latency sketches and a small invocation replaybench to synthesize representative token sequences for validation and alert tuning.

Goal: give SREs and platform engineers a low-cost, queryable summary of per-session latency distributions and a reproducible synthetic generator to exercise hot paths for alert calibration and dashboarding. This supports automated alert dampening and more robust long-tail detection without blowing up storage or cardinality.

What's included (summary):
- New runtime sketch collector: compact reservoir-backed, time-windowed latency sketches keyed by (tenant, route, session_id window). Sketches are optimized for low-allocation hot paths and expose percentiles + tail-mass estimates.
- Replaybench CLI + Python harness: generates synthetic invocations (token timing, token sizes, kv-cache states) from historical traces or randomized shingled bootstraps to validate SLOs and CI jobs.
- Minor server-side ingestion path: lightweight proto for session-sketch telemetry and conversion to rollups stored in the metrics pipeline.
- Grafana dashboard and alert rule examples: session-latency-overview dashboard with cohorting controls and a new alert template that uses session sketch tails for alerting instead of raw p95/p99 spikes.
- Tests: unit tests for sketch ingestion + deterministic replaybench integration tests.
- Docs: observability guide for using sketches + replaybench and recommended alert thresholds.

- [x] Performance microbench: <5% added p50 CPU on the metrics emitter in high-throughput path

Implementation notes:
- The sketch uses a bounded reservoir with exponential decay for recency weighting and a separate compact q-digest to summarize tail mass. This lets us cheaply answer p50/p90/p95/p99 and estimate the % of tokens above a configurable latency bucket.
- Session windows are configurable: default 60s tumbling windows, configurable per-route. We attach a small 16-byte session window ID hash to metrics to keep cardinality modest.
- The replaybench emits sequences with token inter-arrival times and token lengths; the harness can replay against both the runtime (via a local loopback) and the sampling ingest path to validate histogram/sketch consistency.

heterogeneous-attention-fusion-with-staged-scheduler-and-continuous-batching-support

Motivation: reduce p99 latency regression for mixed-sequence workloads and improve throughput for production chat and retrieval runtimes by selecting optimal attention kernels at runtime and enabling continuous batching without sacrificing KV cache hit stability.

Changes: Introduces a heterogeneous attention selection layer (HeteroAttn) that picks between a low-latency microkernel and a high-throughput Flash-like kernel based on sequence length heuristics and current queueing pressure; adds a staged scheduler that enforces a short-term reservation window for latency-sensitive requests and a batch-aggregation window for throughput requests; implements a cooperative KV cache eviction policy (staged LRU) that works with continuous batching to avoid repeated cache thrash during rollups; adds fused rotary/rope offset precomputation paths that avoid memcpy for common rotary patterns; integrates fp16 accumulation path with optional fp32 fallback for edge-case stability; exposes runtime knobs: ATTEN_SELECT_WINDOW_MS, KV_STAGED_WINDOW, CBATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS for tuned rollouts.

Testing and validation: microbenchmarked on c6i-gpu clusters and internal perf-lab; added synthetic mixed-sequence workload harness and end-to-end chat replay traces.

Results: median latency improved 6-9% on mid-sized seqs, p99 reduced up to 22% for mixed workloads, throughput increased 12% on long-sequence tails while KV miss rate decreased 18% under continuous batching.

Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool alpha -> 50% traffic after 72h, automatic rollback on p99 regressions >10% or error rate increase >0.5%.

Backwards compatibility: no API changes.

Known limitations: rare fp16 accumulation differences at extreme sequence lengths (documented and guarded by runtime flag), scheduler parameters tuned for our standard clusters; customers on small on-prem may require adjustments.

runtime: hybrid kernel fallback with KV-consistency gating and safe-mode thresholds

Motivation: intermittent correctness regressions and rare kernel assertion OOMs during long-sequence continuous-batching workloads were being handled by an all-or-nothing safe-mode that fell back to FP32 CPU execution. That approach eliminated correctness incidents but caused large tail latency and cost spikes. This PR implements a hybrid fallback that trades small latency regressions for correctness while keeping most requests on the fast GPU path.

What this change does (single-line summary): Adds a gate that triggers a controlled fallback to compatible kernels (FP32 or CPU) when a set of runtime signals indicate likely correctness risk: KV cache checksum mismatch, kernel assert counter > threshold, or per-request token-level divergence above configured tolerance. The gate is conservative by default and behind a feature flag `hybrid_kernel_fallback` set to off in main; rollout configuration and safe defaults are included.

Key components in the diff (high-level):
- runtime/fallback/hybrid_gate.cc/h: new gate logic that aggregates signals, applies hysteresis and cooldown windows.
- runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc: exposes compatibility metadata and fallback candidates per model artifact.
- runtime/kv/consistency_checker.cc: lightweight KV prefix checksum hooks and sample counters.
- scheduler/continuous_batching_manager.cc: emits per-batch KV stability stats and integrates cooldown decisions.
- observability/metrics.yaml: new metrics: fallback_rate, kv_inconsistency_count, fallback_cooldown_seconds, fallback_latency_penalty.
- integration tests: tests/runtime/hybrid_fallback_integration_test.py: e2e scenarios with long sequences and simulated kernel asserts.
- docs/operational/fallbacks.md: rollout and runbook updates.

Commits (summary):
- 1/6 Add gate primitives and API for aggregated signals
- 2/6 Implement KV checksum sampler and lightweight counter
- 3/6 Hook gate into continuous batching manager and kernel selector
- 4/6 Add metrics and dashboards for visibility
- 5/6 E2E tests and deterministic replay harness
- 6/6 Docs and feature-flagging + rollout config

Testing and CI: Unit tests for gate logic and KV sampler were added. E2E integration tests were flaky at first due to nondeterministic replaying of kernel asserts; added deterministic random seeds and a 'test-only' bypass for timing. CI pipeline initially failed 2 runs on integration tests; failures traced to timing races in the test harness and fixed in commit 5. Final CI status: pass (build + unit + integration + lint).

Perf and correctness numbers from canary (10% traffic in staging for 48h):
- Correctness incident rate: down 93% (from 15 incidents to 1)
- Overall median latency: +0.8% (insignificant)
- 95th percentile latency: +8% (due to fallback tail) — mitigations: cooldown and batching-aware fallback reduce this in subsequent rollouts
- Token-level divergence (regression tests): eliminated for sampled workloads
- Unit-cost impact: +4% at 10% traffic; expected to be neutral at scale with further tuning of thresholds

Rollout plan: feature-flag off in main. Canary -> 10% for 48h (done) -> 50% for 72h (monitor fallback_rate and fallback_latency_penalty) -> 100% if no regression. Alert thresholds added: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained triggers on-call, fallback_latency_penalty > 15% triggers rollback.

Back-and-forth in review (high level):
- Miguel Alvarez: requested stronger telemetry (per-model fallback_rate) and a new metric for 'fallback_reason' tag. Author: added per-model tags and expanded runbook.
- Sofia Chen: flagged potential double-accounting of KV checks when multiple batches mutate same KV; requested a cooldown hysteresis change from 30s->60s. Author: implemented 60s default but left param configurable.
- Derek Wong: requested an e2e test that simulates rapid switchback scenarios; author added an additional integration test and a 'no switchback' policy toggle.

Author notes and rationale: We prefer a conservative hybrid approach that preserves correctness without wholesale safe-mode fallbacks. The gate aggregates cheap signals that are already collected or cost <1% of request time. The tuning parameters (checksum sample rate, hysteresis windows, divergence tolerance) are exposed and documented. The default behavior offline is to be conservative; operators can enable a more aggressive mode for lower cost at their own risk.

Files changed count: 12. Notable small snippets included in runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc to avoid breaking ABI; kernel metadata additions are backward compatible. Integration tests added are deterministic and run in CI with fixed seeds.

Merge and deploy: Approved by reviewers after two rounds of changes. Merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Feature flagged off by default; ops aware via runbook and dashboard. Follow-ups: a follow-up PR will add automatic threshold tuning based on workload profiles (ENG-5410).

proactive KV priming and decode-slip adjuster to reduce tail latency

Motivation: reduce 95th/99th token latency caused by late KV cache population and stage slip (variable prefill->decode handover).

This PR implements a predictive, lightweight KV priming path plus a decode-slip adjuster that dynamically shifts decode scheduling windows to absorb jitter between prefill micro-batches and decode slices.

Key ideas: 1) small, speculative KV priming requests for hot key prefixes predicted from client routing heuristics and recent sequence templates; 2) micro-merge of adjacent KV priming fragments to reduce request spikes when multiple tiny prefill segments target nearby KV pages; 3) decode-slip adjuster that measures micro-latency drift and advances or delays decode worker wakeups to reduce stall probability; 4) runtime toggle flags to enable/disable priming per model/profile and conservative fallbacks to existing prefill pipeline.

This avoids wholesale rework of prefill/decode handoff while gaining measurable tail improvements.

If priming causes net extra GPU work we'll lose overall throughput.

Asha Kapoor: Predictor is intentionally conservative; it first runs on small hashed prefix sketch (cost <1% CPU) and only enqueues priming when predicted confidence > 0.6.

Priming uses lightweight 'kv-read-ahead' which hits the cache layer, not the model kernels, so GPU work is unchanged.

Please add a guard for models with very short contexts (seq_len <= 32) to avoid noisy priming.

Asha Kapoor: Added short-context guard and unit test (see last commit).

Default set to 5ms after experiments (see benchmark_summary).

With KV priming + slip adjuster (default config): p95 token latency = 88ms (-21%), p99 = 156ms (-23%), tail-stall events (stalls > 250ms) reduced by 62%

Introduce SLO Tenor and Sticky Restore Conductor for safer regional restores

Context: Recent incidents showed oscillating regional restores where immediate reopen of circuits and aggressive rejoin caused repeat SLO violations.

This PR introduces a new SLO Tenor concept (time-based soft window) plus a Sticky Restore Conductor to coordinate regional restores and reduce flapping.

Goals: 1) reduce restore-induced SLO spikes by introducing a configurable tenor window that delays aggressive reconnection and reheats KV-preserve policies; 2) provide a sticky restore conductor that centralizes decisioning for per-region restores, with telemetry hooks for post-restore analysis; 3) add a deferred probe hedging mechanism to avoid simultaneous heavy probe storms during restores; 4) safe rollout with feature flag, metrics, and rollback path.

Changeset summary: high-level design + implementation and tests.

Checklist: [x] design doc (ENG-4821) updated; [x] unit + integration tests added; [x] telemetry + dashboards added; [x] feature-flagged behind slo_tenor.enable; [x] rollout plan and rollback notes included.

How it works: SLO Tenor: a tunable duration attached to region-level restores that enforces a soft backoff before allowing full traffic rejoin; the conductor keeps a per-region state (sticky) that remembers last-restore epoch and prevents reopens within tenor unless explicit override; deferred probe hedge: when a restore is started, short randomized probe delays and gentle probe pacing are applied to avoid synchronized load on warm caches.

Rollout plan: canary in us-east-1 with slo_tenor.enable=true and default tenor=60s; monitor 95/99 latency and token cost; after 72h expand across regions.

Rollback: slo_tenor.enable=false or set tenor=0.

Motivation: our presubmit and lint/test pipelines have accrued a lot of language-specific runners and duplicated setup steps. This PR extracts a small, language-agnostic CI adapter layer (Go) and a lightweight dependency-visibility gateway that centralizes dev-dependency detection, stale-lock telemetry, and a permissive gate for fastpath merges. ephemeral-health-gate: cohort-based quiet-window and auto-resolve for circuit stability

Motivation: We continue to see noisy circuit flips in islanded regions during transient backend blips which cause rapid reopen/close churn and SLO spikes for tail latency. This churn also propagates to downstream routing decisions and makes capacity autoscalers overreact. This PR introduces an ephemeral health gate that groups circuits into lightweight cohorts and applies a short consensus quiet-window before allowing reopen transitions. The feature is guarded behind a runtime flag (default: off) and is intended for staged rollouts to Dedicated/Private deployments.

What this changes: 1) cohort builder: lightweight hashing that groups circuits by region+model+capacity-class so that short-lived flaps are evaluated at cohort level instead of per-circuit. 2) consensus quiet-window: when a circuit transitions to open, reopening requires a quorum of cohort members to report healthy for a configurable quiet_window_ms to avoid single-node noisy reopen. 3) soft-lease on circuits: reopened circuits obtain a soft-lease which decays if the cohort health remains marginal — this prevents immediate re-eviction storm. 4) autosolve flow: a periodic reconciler reevaluates cohort health and will progressively restore circuits in small batches if conditions are met. 5) metrics + debugging: new metrics (cohort_health_score, cohort_quiet_window_hits, cohort_reopen_batches) and a console dashboard JSON to visualize cohort state and recent quiet-window events. 6) hotfix: fixes a race in circuit snapshot restore where metrics timestamps could be nil causing occasional panics during node restart.

Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag redwood.experimental.ephemeral_health_gate; staged canary in eu-west-1 on Dedicated for 48h, promote to remaining Dedicated clusters if cohort_health_score stays > 0.95 and no SLO regressions observed. If increased reopen churn is detected, the reconciler supports auto-rollback.

Compatibility and config: default behavior does not alter existing circuit semantics unless the flag is enabled. Config knobs added to runtime/config: cohort_size_hint, quiet_window_ms, reopen_quorum_pct, soft_lease_ms, and batch_restore_size.

Testing: added unit tests for consensus math and cohort builder, integration test simulating transient flaps and verifying cohort-level damping, and a canary script used during manual rollout.

Reduce CI costs with test-slicing, sparse-checkout and dependency-minimizer

Motivation: CI costs and queue times have grown with the test matrix and the monorepo size. This PR introduces three coordinated changes to reduce CI runtime and cache pressure: (1) test-slicing: split integration/unit suites into deterministic shards by changed modules, (2) sparse-checkout in CI runners to limit workspace files downloaded for each job, and (3) dep-minimizer: a lightweight analysis tool that prunes unrelated dependency versions from the effective dependency set used for install caches.

Summary of changes: Added a test-slicing executor (tools/test-slicer) with heuristics for affected-package detection and deterministic shard assignment. Updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to run lightweight changed-file detection as a short-circuit step and only spin up full runners when needed. Integrated sparse-checkout logic into the checkout step to reduce workspace size for long tests. Added infra/dep-minimizer which analyzes lockfiles and module imports to produce a reduced lock overlay used only for CI, keeping production lockfiles untouched.

Why this is safe: All changes are opt-in and guarded by repository config flags (ci.test_slicing.enabled, ci.sparse_checkout.enabled, ci.dep_minimizer.enabled). The dep-minimizer outputs a diagnostics report and cannot be enabled unless a repo admin flips the flag. Test-slicing preserves global test order determinism by seeding shard assignment with repository-wide salt and PR number.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for the test-slicer and dep-minimizer are included. The workflow contains a smoke job that runs a full-suite against a preserved baseline when the config is changed. In this PR the smoke job was run twice against main and head to validate parity. CI run summary appears in checks_summary.

Compatibility notes: No library API changes. Developers will notice faster pre-merge feedback and smaller checkout times in CI. Teams that rely on full workspace integration tests should opt into slicing gradually; docs/ci/onboarding.md includes migration steps and troubleshooting.

Introduce bandwidth provisioning floor and graceful surge compactor

Motivation: large tenants on Dedicated occasionally produce short high-throughput spikes that exhaust ephemeral headroom and cause downstream tail latency spikes. Existing burst token models and warm pools reduce long tail events but are either too coarse or slow to react for sub-30s surges. This PR introduces two orthogonal controls: (1) a configurable bandwidth provisioning floor that guarantees a minimal steady reservation per pool, and (2) a graceful 'surge compactor' daemon that temporarily compacts short-lived requests into a pacing envelope to avoid immediate allocation churn.

What this PR does: Implements a bandwidth_floor allocator that reserves a minimal baseline of GPU/slot tokens per tenant pool scaled by historical 50th-percentile throughput. Adds surge_compactor that intercepts short bursts (default 15s window) and paces allocations with a best-effort compaction ratio to preserve latency SLOs while avoiding over-committing transient capacity. Exposes configs: dedicated.config.bandwidth_floor.{enabled,fraction,min_tokens} and autoscaler.compactor.{enabled,window_secs,max_compact_ratio}.

Design notes: - Floor is additive to existing reservation logic and is applied during provisioning and refill cycles so it does not permanently increase cluster target size; it acts as a soft floor with decay. - Compactor acts inline in the allocation pipeline; it only delays and batches ephemeral requests rather than rejecting them. It emits decision telemetry for later tuning. - Both components are opt-in and default to off for safety.

Telemetry & observability: - New metrics: dedicated.bandwidth_floor.tokens_reserved, autoscaler.compactor.compaction_ratio, autoscaler.compactor.suppressed_requests, dedicated.pool.floor_decay_events. - Dashboards: added a compacting vs direct-allocation split on the Dedicated allocation dashboard. - Traces: compactor decision path annotated for p99 investigation.

Testing & validation: unit tests for allocator math, e2e regression harness that simulates 10–200 concurrent short bursts, and canary in 'staging-dedicated' with synthetic traffic generator. Load testing shows a 42% reduction in ephemeral headroom churn and median latency unchanged; 95th p99 improved under high microburst scenarios by ~8%.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; configs default to disabled. 2) Enable floor in staging on a single tenant pool and observe headroom/latency metrics for 48h. 3) Enable compactor in canary with max_compact_ratio=0.5, monitor suppressed_requests and SLOs for 72h. 4) Gradually increase coverage and compile a tuning recipe for common workloads.

Compatibility & migration: No migration required. All changes are feature-flagged and backward compatible. If compactor causes unexpected behavior it can be fully disabled at runtime.

Security & perf considerations: Compactor is CPU-light but touches allocation hot-path; microbenchmarks show <2% added latency to allocation tail in no-op mode. We instrumented token accounting to ensure no double-counting of reservations.

staged-multi-arm-traffic-reconciler-with-timestamped-cohort-leases

Summary: Introduces a staged multi-arm traffic reconciler that coordinates timed cohort leases and deterministic reconciliation to support multi-variant canaries, A/B experiments, and shadow-to-canary promotions with safe automatic rollback windows.

Motivation: Current rollout controller optimizes single-path canaries but struggles when multiple concurrent arms (A/B/n) need coordinated swaps, timed lease expiry, and deterministic conflict resolution across regions and Dedicated clusters.

This PR implements a lease-based temporal reconciler that: 1) assigns timestamped leases to cohort partitions, 2) uses a conflict-free reconciliation loop to avoid oscillation when multiple controllers observe different states, 3) provides a promotion API for shadow arms to be fast-swapped into serving lanes when metric gates pass, and 4) exposes fine-grained probe hooks for safety gates and automatic rollback triggers.

Design highlights: - Lease model: cohorts receive monotonic timestamped leases (lease_id + expiry_ts).

A reconciler accepts an action only when local time < expiry_ts and lease origin matches expected coordinator. - Deterministic reconciliation: deterministic tie-breaker (lease_id + origin priority) prevents flip-flop across regions when controller heartbeats cross. - Multi-arm state machine: supports an arbitrary number of arms, tracks per-arm telemetry windows, and allows staged promotion where arm B can be promoted to 30% then 60% with automatic safety holdpoints. - Shadow promotion: a shadow arm can be promoted into live traffic via promoteShadow API; traffic migrates through an atomic staged plan that respects session affinity and KV-cache compatibility checks. - Rollback orchestration: rollback plans are checkpointed; a heuristic auto-rollback triggers on SLO/mortality gates with a configurable grace window and therapeutical cool-down to avoid thrashing.

Auto-stop/rollback canary rollouts on SLO breach (Hosted)

Context
We’re adding GA-grade safety mechanisms to Hosted canary rollouts: if the canary cohort regresses on key SLO signals, automatically stop the rollout and either pause or rollback depending on policy. This PR wires stop-condition evaluation into the rollout orchestrator loop and adds notification hooks so customers + on-call can see what happened.

What’s included
- Stop condition evaluation service (server-side) that continuously evaluates cohort metrics for the current step and emits a decision: CONTINUE | PAUSE | ROLLBACK.
- Policy-driven thresholds (initial defaults) for:
  - 5xx rate regression (absolute + relative)
  - timeout rate regression
  - p95 latency regression
- Minimum sample / warmup guardrails to avoid flapping on low traffic:
  - min_requests_per_cohort
  - min_eval_window_seconds
- Orchestrator integration:
  - Runs evaluator periodically while a step is in SOAKING state
  - On breach: transitions rollout state, persists reason, emits activity timeline event
  - Rollback path sets traffic split to baseline=100%, canary=0% and marks rollout ROLLED_BACK
  - Pause path freezes split at current % and marks step PAUSED
- Notifications:
  - Console event stream: `rollout.auto_paused` / `rollout.auto_rolled_back` with structured reason payload
  - PagerDuty routing via existing SRE notifier (gated to beta tenants; see notes)
  - Email/webhook fanout via control-plane notification bus (best-effort)
- Telemetry:
  - Metrics for evaluation duration, evaluation errors, and number of auto-pauses/rollbacks by tenant/route
  - Adds a “stop_condition” tag (bounded enum) for rollouts events (no high-cardinality rollout_id in metrics; rollout_id remains in logs)

Out of scope
- Quality gates as hard blockers (we allow optional manual quality signals but no automated eval integration here)
- Dedicated/Private wiring (schema is shared; enforcement is Hosted-only)

Out of scope
- Quality gates as hard blockers (we allow optional manual quality signals but no automated eval integration here)
- Dedicated/Private wiring (schema is shared; enforcement is Hosted-only)

Implementation notes
- Evaluator queries cohort aggregates from telemetry service (ENG-9152) using a fixed set of dimensions (tenant_id, route_id, cohort, region). For this PR, evaluation is done per-region, then combined using a conservative rule: if any region breaches, trigger action.
- Threshold semantics:
  - latency_p95_regression: triggers when canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * (1 + relative_regression) AND canary_p95 > baseline_p95 + absolute_ms
  - error_rate_5xx_regression: triggers when canary_5xx_rate > baseline_5xx_rate + absolute_pp OR canary_5xx_rate > baseline_5xx_rate * (1 + relative_regression)
  - timeout_rate_regression: same structure as 5xx
- State machine changes are additive and backwards compatible: stop-condition actions only apply to steps with `stop_conditions` configured; otherwise behavior is unchanged.

Testing
- Unit tests for threshold comparisons and min-sample logic
- Orchestrator state machine tests:
  - SOAKING -> AUTO_PAUSED
  - SOAKING -> AUTO_ROLLED_BACK
  - No action when below min sample/window
- Integration test in staging (manual) using synthetic error injection in canary cohort

Rollout / risk
- Feature-flagged behind `hosted_canary_auto_stop_enabled` (default off) and only enabled for beta tenants.
- PagerDuty alerting is additionally gated behind `hosted_canary_auto_stop_paging_enabled` to avoid beta alert storms.

Follow-ups
- Add evaluation timeout handling + retries (currently evaluator returns an error and we keep soaking; will tighten before GA)
- Expose stop-condition configuration UI in Console wizard (currently API-only; Console shows read-only reason/events)

Refs

- Related PRs: pr-28788 (orchestrator), pr-28819 (cohort tagging), pr-28910 (dashboards/templates)
- Runbook draft: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split

Add top-k tail-risk canary detector + adaptive quorum rollout guard

Context and motivation: We have recurring incidents where small fractions of traffic exhibit severe tail latency (p99.99+) after model or runtime changes. Existing detectors (percentile fusion, temporal cohorts) flag broad regressions but often miss concentrated tail risk that affects a tiny slice yet can cause downstream failures. This PR introduces a Top-K Tail-Risk detector that explicitly measures concentrated extreme latency events across stratified traffic slices and an adaptive quorum rollout guard that requires a configurable fraction of slices to agree on degradation before blocking a rollout.

What this change does: Implements a probabilistic tail-risk scoring algorithm (inspired by EVT-style peak-over-threshold combined with Top-K frequency aggregation) that: 1) computes per-slice extreme-event counts over time windows, 2) normalizes by baseline traffic to surface concentrated bursts, and 3) produces a confidence score and suggested mitigation severity. The adaptive quorum guard consumes these signals and enforces policy rules in the rollout controller: quorum policies are configurable by SLO weight, minimum-slice coverage, and hysteresis cooldown.

Why this approach: Concentrated tail events (e.g., 0.1% of requests with very long latencies) can cascade into queuing amplification and throughput collapse when retries or autoscaling kicks in. By focusing on the Top-K extreme samples and requiring cross-slice consensus, we reduce false positives from noisy single-slice blips while catching real, high-impact regressions earlier.

Compatibility and scope: The detector plugs into the existing perf-canary pipeline (ingest -> slice-aggregator -> detectors -> orchestrator). No changes to runtime inference path are required. Defaults are conservative: detector disabled by default for non-critical deployments and enabled for Dedicated + Private by the rollout config.

Hybrid signal-attn kernel with rotary-sparsity fusion and KV prefetch scheduler

Motivation: Production workloads exhibit mixed sequence length distributions and intermittent sparsity from rotary/rope quantization artifacts. Existing Flash-style kernels are high-throughput for dense attention but underutilize opportunities where token locality and structured sparsity exist. This PR introduces 'signal-attn', a hybrid kernel that combines a fast-path Flash-like matmul for dense regions and a lightweight sparse-merge engine for rotary-sparsity lanes. The kernel integrates with the serving runtime scheduler using a signal-driven prefetch heuristic for the KV cache and a continuous-batching hint that reduces tail latency without sacrificing throughput.

Summary: Implement a new attention kernel and scheduler hooks that: 1) Detect per-batch rotary-sparsity patterns (simple entropy+mask heuristics) and route attention work to either dense or hybrid execution path. 2) Fuse rotary/rope application into the QKV projection pipeline to avoid an extra transpose+allocate in the hot path. 3) Add KV prefetch scheduler hints that prioritize hot shards and stagger prefetch to avoid PCIe contention under bursty arrival patterns. 4) Expose a runtime config flag to tune the hybrid threshold and continuous-batcher latency budget.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on p4d-like instance (A100 style) with representative models: - 7B dense: 15% throughput increase, 12% median latency reduction, 9% p99 reduction. - 13B mixed-length: 22% throughput increase, 17% median latency reduction, 18% p99 reduction. - 70B semi-sparse eval (synth rope sparsity): 25% throughput uplift on best-effort routing, 23% p99 reduction after warm-up. End-to-end synthetic RLHF workload saw a 14% token-cost reduction due to fewer recomputations and better batching. Full benchmark logs attached in artifacts.

Small API additions: config flag --attn.hybrid_threshold, --attn.kv_prefetch_window_ms.

Compatibility and safety: The hybrid path is opt-in by default and gated behind runtime config and per-model capability checks. Numeric stability tests (fp16/fp32) were added; all existing attention unit tests remain unchanged and pass. The kernel falls back to the dense Flash-compatible path if the mask/entropy heuristic is inconclusive or if quantized kernels are required.

Review notes: This PR intentionally keeps the rotor/rope fusion local to the attention hot path to avoid changing serialized model weights or checkpoints; only runtime transient transforms are applied. The rotary fuse uses aliasing-friendly in-place transforms to minimize extra allocations. The KV prefetcher introduces conservative heuristics first, with a progressive rollout via the continuous-batcher budget parameter to reduce the risk of PCIe saturation.

econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults

Title: econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults.

Summary: Adds a developer-facing CLI and small platform hooks to run a fast, local 'econ sandbox' that simulates tenant request shapes against candidate batching, cache warmup, and quantization profiles and outputs recommended defaults and unit-econ estimates.

Motivation: Teams repeatedly run ad-hoc scripts to tune batching, cache prefill, and quantization for new tenants.

This PR formalizes a lightweight sandbox that codifies the heuristics we use in production autotuners so engineers can iterate faster and generate reproducible suggestions tailored to tenant traffic patterns.

The tool is intended to accelerate onboarding of Dedicated/Private customers and reduce manual tuning work that currently costs engineering time and leads to suboptimal unit economics.

What this changes: 1) New CLI command: redwood econ sandbox run --profile=<yaml> --dry-run|--apply which loads a small YAML workload signature and candidate profile list, runs a fast probabilistic simulation and returns ranked recommendations with estimated token-cost and p95 latency impact.

2) New config schema: /configs/econ/sandbox-profiles/*.yaml (three sample profiles added: conservative, balanced, aggressive).

3) Telemetry additions: econ.sandbox.recommendation_score, econ.sandbox.simulated_p50_ms, econ.sandbox.simulated_p95_ms, econ.sandbox.estimated_cost_tokens.

4) Safety gate: recommendations flagged with a latency-risk tag if simulated p95 exceeds the target SLO; these recommendations are excluded from --apply unless --force is passed.

5) Small API surface: a sandbox runner library under pkg/econ/sandbox that can be reused by the existing autotuner and by integration tests.

6) E2E smoke test and a new unit-econ regression test in ci/econ that validates scoring stability over a canonical trace.

Implementation notes: The simulator is intentionally approximate: it uses an event-driven, light-weight replay that models batching dynamics, KV-cache hit rates (with configurable prefix skew), and quantization model latency profiles (sampled from per-device latency histograms).

It supports 'dry-run' mode that emits a JSON recommendation bundle and a human-readable summary.

The CLI also supports --compare <baseline-id> to diff the proposed defaults against an existing tenant profile.

thresholded-shadow-canary-orchestration-with-quarantine

Motivation: production model promotion needs deterministic, metric-driven promotion and a lightweight quarantine path for problematic variants without full rollback noise.

This PR implements a thresholded shadow->canary promotion flow and a quarantine first-class primitive that isolates models showing drift or error spikes.

Changes include: new rollout controller state machine, metric threshold DSL, quarantine API surface, deterministic warmup windows, and end-to-end integration with the observability stack and canary alerts.

Design highlights: 1) Shadow priming stage: route mirrored traffic to candidate model while keeping responses hidden; automatic delta metrics (latency, token-err, perplexity, hallucination-score) computed over sampling windows.

2) Threshold evaluation: a compact DSL in rollout config allows percentage and absolute thresholds with lookback windows (e.g., latency_p95<120ms AND token_err_rate_delta<0.5%).

3) Canary promotion: automated gradual traffic bump with hold windows and automated rollback if thresholds violated.

4) Quarantine: when a threshold breach occurs during shadow or canary, the controller moves the variant to 'quarantined' state, which preserves logs, stops routing live traffic, and spins a lightweight readonly debug endpoint for replaying failing traces.

5) Safety: automatic cooldowns, explicit owner notifications, and a manual override to promote from quarantine after investigation.

This description includes the user-visible rollout configuration changes and the operational playbook.

stream-facade-lightweight-cred-fallback-and-backoff-profiles

Context and motivation: Multiple downstream teams reported friction when migrating from push-based stream handlers to more ergonomic pull-iterators and when rotating short-lived credentials in multi-tenant setups.

This PR introduces a small, pluggable streaming facade (pull-iterator API) surfaced by the redwood runtime and SDK adapters, a credential-fallback mesh that lets SDKs fall back through a prioritized chain (env -> host-proxy -> refresh-token-provider) without surface changes to application code, and a set of named backoff profiles (fast/standard/steady) to simplify retry ergonomics.

Checklist: - [x] Implement pull-style streaming facade in the runtime shim - [x] Add thin adapter implementations in go/ts/python SDK layers - [x] Credential fallback chain with clear opt-out - [x] Add named backoff profiles + telemetry hooks - [x] Update docs, examples, and changelog - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests and local e2e run Commits summary: commit 1: add streaming facade interface and initial runtime bridge; commit 2: implement credential fallback mesh and priority resolver; commit 3: add backoff profile registry and default policy; commit 4: SDK adapters (go/ts/python) and small portability shims; commit 5: tests, docs, and changelog updates.

Changed areas/files (high level): - runtime/streaming/facade.go: new lightweight facade and interface adapters - runtime/auth/fallback_resolver.go: prioritized credential chain - sdk/go/adapter/pullstream.go: go-side adapter and examples - sdk/ts/src/pullIteratorAdapter.ts: typescript adapter + typed examples - sdk/python/redwood/pull_stream.py: python pull iterator shim - docs/sdk/streaming.md: design and migration guide - tests/integration/stream_pull_e2e: cross-sdk e2e harness Notable implementation details: the facade is intentionally minimal (Next()/peek token semantics) to avoid coupling to transport changes; the credential mesh resolves providers in order and only uses the next provider if the previous returns a 401 or expired-token sentinel; backoff profiles are parameterized (initial_ms, max_ms, multiplier, jitter) and registered centrally to ensure parity across SDKs.

Review conversation highlights: - Sofia: "Can we avoid implicit blocking on Next() for sync SDKs?" Author reply: "The adapter exposes both async and sync wrappers; sync callers get a small bounded worker that buffers 1 item to avoid unbounded blocking." - Miguel: "Telemetry hooks need callsite labels for batching vs single-token flows." Author: "Added 'stream.kind' tag and unit tests." - Ava: "Do we risk credential leakage when proxying fallback providers?" Author: "The mesh enforces a single in-memory token cache per request scope and optionally emits audit events; documented and opt-outtable." CI and testing: initial CI run flagged lint failures in the TS adapter; those were fixed in commit 4.

Integration matrix run passed across go1.21, node18, python3.11 matrices.

Flaky test observed in e2e harness (stream termination race) and mitigated by adding a small grace window and idempotent close semantics.

Performance and compatibility notes: microbenchmarks show the facade adds ~0.8-1.4% CPU overhead on steady throughput but simplifies caller code and avoids complex coroutine juggling.

Compatibility layer ensures existing push-based streaming clients continue to work; new API is additive.

Migration notes: documented step-by-step guide in docs/sdk/streaming.md and added small examples in sdk/*/examples/pullstream.

Security and privacy: credential fallback respects KMS boundaries and never logs token material; audit events are opt-in.

Release plan: included in next patch SDK release cycle; manual migration guidance and an automated codemod for TypeScript added under tools/codemods.

Merge outcome: PR was approved by all reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-04 after green CI.

Related work: follows up on ENG-7541 (stream ergonomics spike) and pairs with a future runtime scheduling change (ENG-9620).

Introduce a lightweight streaming facade that unifies pull-style iterators across Go/TS/Python, adds a credential fallback mesh for short-lived tokens, and exposes configurable backoff profiles for ergonomic defaults.

Introduce RBACv2 policy synthesizer, KMS usage reviewer, and audit reconciliation job

Motivation: Recent support tickets (SUP-903) and internal postmortem identified two recurring pain points: (1) RBACv2 rollouts often over-provisioned operator bindings leading to unexpected KMS calls crossing geo boundaries; (2) audit logs and KMS access records were not reconciled, making longitudinal investigations slow. This PR ships a three-part solution: a policy synthesizer that emits minimal effective RBAC patches, a KMS usage reviewer that tags KMS calls with derived decision traces and residency flags, and an audit-reconciliation job that cross-checks authz decisions, KMS events, and immutable audit envelopes to flag inconsistencies.

Design summary: - policy/synthesizer: a deterministic pass that consumes role-presets + service-claim annotations and outputs minimal allow-lists (keeps deny semantics untouched). It is implemented as an idempotent compiler stage used by the policy orchestrator during canaries. - kms/reviewer: sidecar-style aggregator (service behind /internal/kms-review) that enriches KMS telemetry with policy-decision-ids, tenant-residency, and operator-scope to enable quota/residency checks. - audit/reconciler: periodic job (configurable cadence) which performs joins across authz_decisions, kms_access_log, and audit_envelopes to produce a per-tenant discrepancy report written to compliance.reconciliations. The job includes a lightweight dedupe and fingerprint algorithm to avoid noisy alerts.

Implementation notes/changes: - new package: internal/policy/synthesizer (Go) with unit tests and fakes for operator presets. - new service: services/kms-reviewer (small Go HTTP service + Prometheus metrics), deployed as a singleton per-region. - migration: add reconciliations table (+ schema v43) to postgres; migration includes backfill script limited to 30 days. - observability: new metrics policy_synth_runs_total, kms_reviewer_calls, reconciler_discrepancies_by_type; tags include tenant_id and region. - ops: added a cron manifest at deploy/cron/reconciler.yaml and a Helm values section to opt-in for high-compliance tenants.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for synthesizer compiler logic
- [x] Integration tests for kms-reviewer enrichment route
- [x] Migration and backfill tested on staging
- [x] Metrics and logs instrumented
- [x] Documentation: docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md and docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md
- [x] Security scan (snyk/gosec) passed after fixing two low-severity findings

Commits (high level): - 1) add synthesizer core + tests - 2) implement kms reviewer service and client shim - 3) add reconciler job + migration - 4) add Helm charts + deploy manifests - 5) docs and runbook - 6) fixes from reviewers (metrics labels, retry tuning)

Changed areas (high level): - internal/policy/synthesizer/* - services/kms-reviewer/{cmd,handlers,metrics} - jobs/reconciler/* - cmd/infra/migrations/043_add_reconciliations.sql - deploy/helm/redwood/templates/cron-reconciler.yaml - docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md - docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md

Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Chu: "Can we avoid an N^2 policy expansion in the synthesizer?" Reply: added a constraint-sweep that limits expansion to cross-service grants only; added tests and a benchmark fixture. - Marta Kaczmarek: "Metrics need tenant and region labels for SLO slicing." Reply: added tenant_id and region labels, instrumented with cardinality guard and sample rate. - Samir Patel: "Make migration backward-compatible for mixed-version clusters." Reply: reconciler backfill is guarded by a feature flag and uses a read-path fallback when reconciliations table is not present.

CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: pass (flaky test fixed in commit 5) - lint: pass - e2e: pass on staging deployment - security-scan: initial fail (gosec findings) -> patched -> pass. Full pipeline passed on rerun.

Operational notes: - Default deployment is opt-in for enterprise tenants via Helm values `reconciler.enabled`. - KMS reviewer runs as a regional singleton to keep cross-tenant telemetry coalesced. - To troubleshoot mismatches, use the new /internal/debug/reconciler endpoint (RBAC-protected) which returns sample joined artifacts for a reconciliation ID.

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged to main. Post-merge: run migration v43 during next maintenance window; operators on Dedicated/Private should coordinate with infra for opt-in. Release note included. If any tenant relies on implicit operator bindings, they should schedule a canary with policy.synth.enabled=false to avoid immediate rollbacks.
Added RBACv2 policy synthesizer (auto-minimization), KMS usage reviewer service, and periodic audit reconciliation job. No API changes to public endpoints. Ops: add new cronjob and a small DB migration.
This PR was intentionally split into small commits to make the security review easier; product/ops are informed. No public SDK changes.
